10A - Risk Scenario Unauthorized Interna.title: Unauthorized (internal) users successfully break into systems.
10A - Risk Scenario Unauthorized Interna.statement: An internal user accesses organizational systems and affects the confidentiality, integrity or availability of assets.

scenario_context.actor: Nonmalicious internal employees, malicious insiders, cybercriminals
scenario_context.intent: Accidental or intentional events caused by (internal) threat actors that can result from a procedure improperly implemented, collusion between employees or lack of proper technical controls implemented. Motivation can include revenge, trying to hide an illegal act previously performed and ceasing (temporary or permanently) the activity of the enterprise.
scenario_context.threat_event: Internal attacker gains access to data or systems pertaining to the enterprise and compromises the confidentiality, integrity or availability of such systems.
scenario_context.assets: Any system or asset that is left vulnerable to external/internal attack due to error, misconfiguration, lack of properly implemented internal procedures or technical controls Any data stored on affected systems System availability
scenario_context.consequence: Consequences depend highly on the type of data affected (e.g., essential for providing services to the customer or not) and on the possibility to swiftly retrieve the data from backups. The consequences can range from minor reputation damages (without material damages to customers) to significant material damages to customers if the services toward them cannot be provided anymore.
scenario_context.timing: Systems being affected when necessary to offer services to a customer may have a higher impact. Detection and timing of the incident can vary greatly on the threat actors skills and resources. The detection depends on the controls in place. If proper controls are not in place, the enterprise may find out about the incident after a long period of time.

impact_dimensions.cost_of_response: Retrieving from backing up the data or trying to recreate the data from other sources in a manual manner
impact_dimensions.replacement_cost: If replacement of IT solution or reinstalling of IT solution is needed.
impact_dimensions.competitive_advantage: If the data are essential for the business purpose of the enterprise, its competitive advantage may be affected
impact_dimensions.reputation: Knowledge of this type of incident negatively affects the enterprises reputation.
impact_dimensions.fines_and_judgements: Fines could be a consequence, depending on the lack of service provision, breach of data protection legislation Judgements can become relevant if customers are impacted by the incident, e.g., services are not provided properly and timely to the customer.

extents.worst_case: The data or systems affected by the employee are essential for the business process and the enterprise does not have a resilience process.
extents.typical_case: The data or systems affected by the employee are essential for the business process. However, there is a manner to retrieve it (e.g., from backups) even if the services provided by the enterprise are affected until this is done.
extents.best_case: The data or systems affected by the employee are not essential for the business process and can easily be retrieved from backups.

mitigating_controls.description: Analyze risk. Periodical risk assessment and risk management in general are essential in order to identify potential risks, their impact and probability, including this risk scenario. This control is at the core of other more specific controls and needed to identify them properly.

Monitor I&T infrastructure. The proper continuous monitoring of the I&T infrastructure ensures that lack of compliance with controls or new types of events (e.g., potential malware, new vulnerabilities) is identified swiftly.

Manage endpoint security. Ensure that endpoints (e.g., laptop, desktop, server, and other mobile and network devices or software) are secured at a level that is equal to or greater than the defined security requirements for the information processed, stored or transmitted.

Manage user identity and logical access. Ensure that all users have information access rights in accordance with business requirements. Coordinate with business units that manage their own access rights within business processes.

Manage roles, responsibilities, access privileges and levels of authority. Manage business roles, responsibilities, levels of authority and segregation of duties needed to support the business process objectives. Authorize access to all information assets related to business information processes, including those under the custody of the business, IT and third parties. This ensures that the business knows where the data are and who is handling data on its behalf.

10B - Risk Scenario Service Interruption.title: Service interruption occurs due to a denial of service attack.
10B - Risk Scenario Service Interruption.statement: A DDoS (distributed denial of service) attack results in performance degradation of organizational websites.

scenario_context.intent: Financial gain: attacker requests ransom to stop the DDoS attack. Reputational harm: attacker targets on disrupting victims services in order to cause reputation harm. Financial harm: attacker targets on disrupting victims services in order to negatively impact victims operations and associated services sales.
scenario_context.threat_event: Attacker typically utilizes Dark Web or other clandestine resources in order to launch a large-scale attack on victims services. Utilization of these resources can provide significant traffic volumes with the necessary dispersion as to be almost impossible to trace back
scenario_context.assets: A wide area of assets can be targeted including web services, cloud services or infrastructure-related services.
scenario_context.consequence: Services disruption could directly affect the enterprises productivity, cost of response and harm reputation in a prolonged scenario.
scenario_context.timing: The duration of the incident can be very short or prolonged. Early detection cold be a key to minimize the impact for a timely response. If the event takes place on business-critical period (e.g. Black Friday for retail industries, last days of an RFP, etc.), it will cause higher impact.

impact_dimensions.cost_of_response: Response costs are present, as incident responders, communications, PR and management meetings work on the incident depending on severity.
impact_dimensions.replacement_cost: In case of a prolonged and very large volume DDoS attack, equipment may need to be repurchased elsewhere.
impact_dimensions.competitive_advantage: If attack takes place on a critical period from a business/sales perspective, competitive advantage is also negatively impacted.
impact_dimensions.reputation: In case of a high volume and prolonged attack, enterprise reputation is also seriously affected.
impact_dimensions.fines_and_judgements: Fines and judgement could be an impact dimension in cases that service disruptions lead to inability to meet SLA times or address data privacy requests.

extents.worst_case: Attack of high magnitude which causes prolonged service disruptions during a business-critical period could affect an enterprises viability.
extents.typical_case: High magnitude attacks during a random period which is not considered business critical
extents.best_case: Low volume attack which causes services degradation or short-period/unnoticed service disruption

10C - Risk Scenario Defaced Website.docx.title: A website is defaced.
10C - Risk Scenario Defaced Website.docx.statement: A flaw in the security of an enterprises website results in a website defacement that creates a security incident for the enterprise.

scenario_context.intent: The intent is to create embarrassment to the enterprise, to damage the enterprises reputation, even more so if the enterprise is in the information security/cybersecurity area, since it could lead to damages in stock price, existing and future clientele as well.
scenario_context.threat_event: The actor(s) is injecting infected code into the sites script, which allows the actor(s) to take control of the website. Afterwards, the actor(s) could potentially gain access privileges to the website and any other content. In addition, using scanning software to find vulnerabilities, actor(s) could potentially access the website through a vulnerability/flaw in the website.
scenario_context.assets: The assets affected are the website and any related servers. Any related information residing on the web server could also potentially be affected as well.
scenario_context.consequence: The reputation of the enterprise is severely impacted and potentially the actor(s) could have gained confidential/sensitive information.
scenario_context.timing: The timing of the defacement could be related to the launch of a new product and/or service of the enterprise, to increase the damage in terms of reputation.

impact_dimensions.cost_of_response: N/A
impact_dimensions.competitive_advantage: N/A
impact_dimensions.reputation: N/A

extents.worst_case: Worst-case scenario is the website is defaced and no one is noticing from the enterprise, until it is already too late and the reputation of the enterprise is severely impacted. Although the website is restored to its previous state, the damage in reputation is already done.
extents.typical_case: Most likely case is the website is defaced and somehow, either internally or externally, the enterprise is becoming aware of the defacement, and they are quickly responding to restore it to its previous state. Whatever damage was done in reputation is handled by the marketing/PR department.
extents.best_case: Best-case scenario is that although the website is defaced, the controls in place managed to identify the actor(s) activities and the IT department of the enterprise have restored the website to its previous states, within a reasonable time frame without any serious impact on the reputation.

10D - Risk Scenario Malware Attack.docx.title: The enterprise experiences a malware attack.
10D - Risk Scenario Malware Attack.docx.statement: A malicious actor infects an enterprises systems with malware, affecting the confidentiality, integrity and availability of assets.

scenario_context.actor: Cyber criminals, Hacktivists and malicious insiders
scenario_context.intent: Malware infections are generally perpetrated by individuals, enterprises or government entities with malicious intent. The goal of malware is usually for financial gain but can include system intrusion, extortion, hacktivism and intentional outages.
scenario_context.threat_event: An attacker gains access to systems using malware and accesses data (confidentiality), modifies data (integrity) or causes outages (availability) on organizational systems.
scenario_context.assets: Any enterprise system or asset Any data stored on affected systems System availability
scenario_context.consequence: Consequences can vary greatly depending on the nature of the attack but may range from full data breach scenarios, extortion and outages via ransomware, credential theft and many other forms of negative impacts.
scenario_context.timing: Systems being affected when necessary to offer services to a customer may have a higher impact. Detection and timing of the incident can vary greatly on the threat actors skills and resources. The detection depends on the controls in place. If proper controls are not in place, the enterprise may find out about the incident after a long period of time.

impact_dimensions.cost_of_response: IT and security teams form the majority of response costs from malware infections, but costs may also arise from legal, PR, comms, executive management and other teams if the incident is far reaching and impacts many teams or customers (e.g., ransomware, data breaches).
impact_dimensions.replacement_cost: Systems could be completely replaced if the infection is severe enough or completely inaccessible, as the case in some ransomware events.
impact_dimensions.competitive_advantage: If the incident affects customers and is severe enough, competitive advantage may be impacted.
impact_dimensions.reputation: If the incident affects customers and is severe enough, reputation may be impacted.
impact_dimensions.fines_and_judgements: Fines and judgements may be a factor in severe incidents if the enterprise did not adequately protect data and systems.

extents.worst_case: All critical servers in the enterprise are affected. There is no access to critical information. Backups are not performed correctly. Outages and unauthorized data access cause systems to be inoperative for a significant time, threatening the health of the enterprise.
extents.typical_case: Primary servers are affected with malware and the retrieval of information takes a long time, but the enterprise can recover with significant response costs.
extents.best_case: Malware is detected early enough to allow for an early intervention, minimizing damage and costs.

10E - Risk Scenario Industrial Espionage.title: Industrial espionage takes place.
10E - Risk Scenario Industrial Espionage.statement: A foreign state or enterprise hacks the enterprises systems and obtains important and condential product and client information, reducing the enterprises competitive position.

scenario_context.intent: Gain competitors internal information such as intellectual property, strategic plans, pricing and customer list in order to be utilized in advance of the attacker state or enterprise
scenario_context.threat_event: Attacker gains access to enterprise internal network by exploiting a perimeter vulnerability or using social engineering techniques. Usually, successful attacks require detailed planning and short lateral movement each time so as to not be identified, resulting in a prolonged event.
scenario_context.assets: Human and technical assets are involved and an enterprises confidential and internal information.
scenario_context.consequence: The major consequence is the loss of competitive advantage for the victim.
scenario_context.timing: Impact could be higher if the cyber espionage event takes place prior to a product release or prior to the design of new strategic plans.

impact_dimensions.cost_of_response: Response costs are present, as incident responders, communications, PR, management meetings, forensics, etc. work on the incident depending on severity.
impact_dimensions.replacement_cost: Replacement cost in terms of replacing enterprise plans in order to regain the competitive advantage
impact_dimensions.competitive_advantage: Competitive advantage is significantly affected since competitor becomes fully aware of enterprises internal information and plans.
impact_dimensions.reputation: Reputation is affected if information regarding the hack incident is leaked into the media.
impact_dimensions.fines_and_judgements: If the hack includes personal data, regulatory fines may be imposed. Furthermore, if the hack includes third-party intellectual property, legal action may be raised by the affected third party.

extents.worst_case: A competitor gains data that are critical for the enterprises viability. Such data include intellectual property, pending patents, source code, customers price lists, risk register, and strategic plans. Competitor takes advantage in a full scale and target enterprise loses a significant market share.
extents.typical_case: Competitor achieves to obtain confidential files such as management presentation, project plans and e-mail communications. The enterprise loses some short-term market share but can recover.
extents.best_case: Competitor achieves to obtain internal documents (policies/procedures/forms) and information that cannot be utilized for gaining competitive advantage.

10F - Risk Scenario Hacking.docx.title: Hacktivism occurs.
10F - Risk Scenario Hacking.docx.statement: A hacktivist seeks to send a political or social message to a target enterprise or the public and launch an attack that affects the confidentiality, integrity or availability of systems.

scenario_context.intent: Pressure business to change their practice or immediate financial gain; send a larger political message to the public.
scenario_context.threat_event: Hacktivists can affect the confidentiality and integrity of systems by defacing websites, compromising social media accounts and other forms of attacks. Availability attacks can be launched via ransomware, extortion and DDoS attacks.
scenario_context.assets: Human and technical assets are involved and an enterprises confidential and internal information.

extents.best_case: Any activity that indicates try to gain access to sensitive information has been detected via Security Monitoring Tools or Threat Intelligence and proper steps have been taken to cease the DDoS attack.

scenario_context.intent: N/A
scenario_context.threat_event: Possible threat events mainly include the exploitation of human factor with the use of social engineering methods combined with distribution of malicious software.
scenario_context.assets: Any organization system or asset Any data stored on affected systems System availability
scenario_context.consequence: Response costs and reputation issues while under certain circumstances; significant costs may include productivity, competitive advantage loss and regulatory fines.
scenario_context.timing: The duration of the incident can be very short or prolonged. Early detection of the data loss is key to minimizing the impact.

extents.best_case: A compromised user account or workstation infection is detected and contained. Bits of enterprise information may be leaked but with no value for the adversary.

10I - Risk Scenario Foreign Government A.title: A foreign government issues attacks on critical systems.
10I - Risk Scenario Foreign Government A.statement: A state-sponsored attacker gains access to systems via cyberattack and accesses data (confidentiality), modifies data (integrity) or causes outages (availability) on organizational systems.

scenario_context.intent: Intentional actions aimed at making a service/IT system unavailable, extracting information from an enterprise or changing the data from an IT system in order to produce negative consequences at the national level of the country against which the attack is perpetrated.
scenario_context.threat_event: The possible threat events are varied due to the nature of the event. Threat events include: External attacker causes an unauthorized disclosure of confidential information. External attacker alters confidential information. External attacker causes system outages.
scenario_context.assets: Any system or asset that is left vulnerable to external/internal attack due to error, misconfiguration, lack of properly implemented internal procedures or technical controls Any data stored on affected systems
scenario_context.consequence: Intentional actions aimed at making a service/IT system unavailable, extracting information from an enterprise or changing the data from an IT system in order to produce negative consequences at the national level of the country against which the attack is perpetrated.
scenario_context.timing: Depending on the business purpose, certain periods/moments may increase the impact level for the incident (e.g., high season of sales for an online store). Such types of attacks may be hard to detect and be within the IT systems of the enterprise for a long time before they are identified. This depends on the cyberattack detection controls in place and on the threat intelligence sharing to which the enterprise participates.

impact_dimensions.cost_of_response: Entails significant resources (internal and external) from forensic services, incident response personnel, retrieval of data from backups, PR and communication, legal services, etc.
impact_dimensions.replacement_cost: Depending on the affected IT systems, their reinstallation or replacement may be needed in order to ensure proper business continuity or IT systems that are not infected.
impact_dimensions.competitive_advantage: If data relevant for a competitive advantage are deleted, change or shared with third parties/public, the competitive advantage could also be impacted.
impact_dimensions.reputation: Knowledge of the incident to customers, co-contractors or to the public can impact the reputation of the enterprise.
impact_dimensions.fines_and_judgements: Fines for lack of service provision to customers or for lack of integrity/confidentiality/availability in case of personal data If the customers/co-contractors are affected materially or morally, they can also request damages before the courts of law.

extents.worst_case: All critical IT systems are compromised (e.g., all data are publicly available; all data have been changed and there is no backup system in place).
extents.typical_case: Scenario 1: Some data are made publicly available or made available to certain interested parties. Scenario 2: Some data are unavailable for a sufficient amount of time to cause damages to customers more than a discomfort for not having the services available. Scenario 3: The data are altered by the attacker and the enterprise does not notice this until a customer files a complaint in this respect. This consequence has some impact on the customers and the enterprise has set up a mitigation mechanism to prevent escalation of damages caused to customers.
extents.best_case: Scenario 1: The critical IT system has a short period of unavailability that has a minor consequence for the customers. Scenario 2: The critical IT system has a short period of loss of integrity that has a minor consequence for the customers. In both scenarios, the attack is quickly identified and proper measures are implemented to stop it and prevent future similar incidents.

mitigating_controls.description: Analyze risk. Periodical risk assessment and risk management in general are essential in order to identify potential risks, their impact and probability, including for this risk scenario. This control is at the core of other more specific controls and needed to identify them properly.

Maintain a risk profile. Maintain an inventory of known risk and risk attributes, including expected frequency, potential impact and responses. Document-related resources, capabilities and current control activities related to risk items.

Establish and maintain an ISMS (information security management system). Establish and maintain an ISMS that provides a standard, formal and continuous approach to information security management, enabling secure technology and business processes that are aligned with business requirements.

Define and manage an information security and privacy risk treatment plan. Maintain an information security plan that describes how information security risk is to be managed and aligned with enterprise strategy and enterprise architecture. Ensure that recommendations for implementing security improvements are based on approved business cases, implemented as an integral part of services and solutions development, and operated as an integral part of business operation.
Manage data backup and restore arrangements. Manage availability of critical data to ensure operational continuity.
Resolve and recover from incidents. Document, apply and test the identified solutions or workarounds. Perform recovery actions to restore the I&T-related service.
Define the business continuity policy, objectives and scope. Define business continuity policy and scope, aligned with enterprise and stakeholder objectives, to improve business resilience.

Maintain business resilience. Evaluate business resilience options and choose a cost-effective and viable strategy that ensures enterprise continuity, disaster recovery and incident response in the face of a disaster or other major incident or disruption.

Develop and implement a business continuity response Develop a business continuity plan and disaster recovery plan based on the strategy. Document all procedures necessary for the enterprise to continue critical activities in the event of an incident.

10J - Risk Scenario Sabotage.docx.title: The data center is destroyed by staff (sabotage, etc.).
10J - Risk Scenario Sabotage.docx.statement: The enterprises data center(s) or systems stored at data center(s) are rendered inoperable due to insider sabotage, causing an availability event.

scenario_context.intent: The most likely motivations for such an event are terrorism (the unlawful use violence for political aims) or acting on behalf of a hostile nation with the goal of disrupting the continuity of operations.
scenario_context.threat_event: Threat actors use kinetic means to damage or destroy property at the enterprises data center, causing system outages and potential staff harm of death.
scenario_context.assets: Data center facilities Computing equipment Communications equipment Software and application systems that facilitate the operation of the enterprise Backup equipment Data Human life
scenario_context.consequence: The operation of the enterprise is compromised until the result of system recovery is obtained, with the consequent impossibility of delivering products and services to customers, thereby affecting the reputation of the enterprise for falling into contractual and regulatory breaches. Loss of human life or injury is also a potential consequence.
scenario_context.timing: If the event occurs in a critical period such as the end of the month, it could have a greater impact since it affects even the delivery of financial information to the different stakeholders. Early declaration of a disaster is key so that recovery efforts can be initiated quickly.

impact_dimensions.cost_of_response: An event of this magnitude carries with it high costs to be able to respond appropriately to the different stakeholders after it has occurred.
impact_dimensions.replacement_cost: The enterprise has to incur significant costs to rebuild all affected facilities.
impact_dimensions.competitive_advantage: The interruption in the operations of the enterprise could be taken by the competitors and thus lose the competitive advantage that the enterprise could have had before the event.
impact_dimensions.reputation: The interruption of the enterprise's operations could have an impact on the reputation due to prolonged outages of public-facing systems.
impact_dimensions.fines_and_judgements: The interruption of the enterprise's operations could originate fines and judgements due to the lack of compliance with contractual and regulatory commitments.

extents.worst_case: Data center facilities destroyed. Rebuilding all affected facilities is very difficult. There are no backups. There is no contingency site to use as an alternative. All the critical information of the enterprise was on those facilities. There is no certainty that all information will be retrieved. Human life is lost or people are injured.
extents.typical_case: There are backups, but the recovery time of the information is long. The affected facilities can be rebuilt, but it may take several months to be operational.
extents.best_case: The damage to the facilities is slight. Lost information is easy to recover. The attack did not affect any of the assets/resources related to this risk scenario.

mitigating_controls.description: Direct risk management. Direct the establishment of risk management practices to provide reasonable assurance that I&T risk management practices are appropriate and that actual I&T risk does not exceed the boards risk appetite.
Establish roles and responsibilities. Define and communicate roles and responsibilities for enterprise I&T, including authority levels, responsibilities and accountability.

Identify key IT personnel. Identify key IT personnel. Use knowledge capture (documentation), knowledge sharing, succession planning and staff backup to minimize reliance on a single individual performing a critical job function.
Analyze risk. Develop a substantiated view on actual I&T risk, in support of risk decisions.
Manage data backup and restore arrangements. Manage availability of critical data to ensure operational continuity.

Assess business impact. Identify important services to the enterprise. Map services and resources to business processes and identify business dependencies. Ensure that the impact of unavailable resources is fully agreed on and accepted by the customer. For vital business functions, ensure that availability requirements can be satisfied per service-level agreement.

Maintain business resilience. Evaluate business resilience options and choose a cost-effective and viable strategy that ensures enterprise continuity, disaster recovery and incident response in the face of a disaster or other major incident or disruption.

Develop and implement a business continuity response. Develop a BCP (business continuity plan) and DRP (disaster recovery plan) based on the strategy. Document all procedures necessary for the enterprise to continue critical activities in the event of an incident.

Exercise, test and review the BCP and DRP. Test continuity on a regular basis to exercise plans against predetermined outcomes, uphold business resilience and allow innovative solutions to be developed.
Manage backup arrangements. Maintain availability of business-critical information.

10K - Risk Scenario Stolen Device.docx.title: A device with sensitive data is stolen.
10K - Risk Scenario Stolen Device.docx.statement: An organizational insider or an external attacker steals computing equipment or a storage device containing sensitive data, affecting the confidentiality, integrity and availability of the asset.

scenario_context.intent: Disgruntled employee, who potentially could sell the sensitive financial data to cybercriminal or hacktivists. Devices can also be stolen by opportunistic individuals who will sell the device for the price of the physical asset or for the data.
scenario_context.threat_event: An attacker steals computing equipment and accesses data (confidentiality), modifies data (integrity) or causes outages (availability) on organizational systems.
scenario_context.assets: Any enterprise system or asset Any data stored on affected systems System availability
scenario_context.consequence: Consequences can vary greatly depending on the nature of the attack but may range from full data breach scenarios, extortion and outages, credential theft and many other forms of negative impacts.
scenario_context.timing: Systems being affected when necessary to offer services to a customer may have a higher impact.

impact_dimensions.cost_of_response: IT and security teams form the majority of response costs from malware infections, but costs may also arise from legal, PR, comms, executive management and other teams if the incident is far reaching and impacts many teams or customers.
impact_dimensions.replacement_cost: Stolen equipment needs to be replaced.
impact_dimensions.competitive_advantage: If the incident affects customers and is severe enough, competitive advantage may be impacted.
impact_dimensions.reputation: If the incident affects customers and is severe enough, reputation may be impacted.
impact_dimensions.fines_and_judgements: Fines and judgements may be a factor in severe incidents if the enterprise did not adequately protect data and systems.

extents.worst_case: The worst-case scenario is a major outage of service due to stolen computing equipment, resulting in loss of customers. Major data breach scenarios are also worst case.
extents.typical_case: In typical cases, damage is limited and backups exist of the affected systems. The actor may be fired and possibly the enterprise charges them with theft, if they want to disclose the incident.
extents.best_case: The best-case scenario is that devices are encrypted and inaccessible and system downtime does not occur. The perpetrator is discovered quickly.

scenario_context.intent: An employee negotiated a contract with a critical IT vendor without going through the enterprise's legal or risk review
scenario_context.threat_event: The event is likely to occur in a single event in an enterprise without appropriate risk appetite and tolerance levels. The amount of risk taken to achieve this objective is unknown by the board or senior leadership.
scenario_context.assets: I&T service delivery
scenario_context.consequence: Poor risk management practices allowed excessive financial risk to be taken to meet a service delivery target.
scenario_context.timing: If the risk taken pays the expected dividends, then no negative outcome may result. If poor risk management practices continue, without visibility or oversight from leadership, there may be a significant financial and reputational cost to the enterprise.

impact_dimensions.cost_of_response: The enterprise spends resources to implement a risk program and processes to better manage risk-taking activities that are in line with appetite and tolerance.
impact_dimensions.competitive_advantage: The amount and level of risk taken result in the desired outcomes, but the product and service cost targets and budgets overrun by 25%50% of the original projected costs.
impact_dimensions.reputation: N/A
impact_dimensions.fines_and_judgements: If the negative financial consequences occur in a publicly traded or regulated enterprise, there could be regulatory sanctions or increased scrutiny into risk management practices.

extents.worst_case: The amount and level of risk taken do not result in the desired outcomes and the financial consequences cause serious, long-term repercussions and perhaps even bankruptcy. If the negative financial consequences occur in a publicly traded or regulated enterprise, there could be regulatory sanctions or increased scrutiny into risk management practices.
extents.typical_case: The amount and level of risk taken result in the desired outcomes, but the product and service cost targets and budgets overrun by 25%50% of the original projected costs. The enterprise can recover but spends resources to implement a risk program and processes to ensure this does not happen in the future.
extents.best_case: The amount and level of risk taken result in the desired outcomes with no negative financial consequences.

11C_Risk Scenario Third Party Suppliers..title: Third-party suppliers do not deliver projects as per contractual agreements (any combination of exceeded budgets, quality problems, missing functionality, late delivery)
11C_Risk Scenario Third Party Suppliers..statement: Delays in software xes to the online retail website occur due to software vendors who fail to meet requirements for timeliness and quality.
11C_Risk Scenario Third Party Suppliers..oversight: IT Governance Board Architecture Board Steering Committee (Programs/ Projects) Chief Risk Officer (CRO)

scenario_context.intent: N/A
scenario_context.threat_event: The event is unlikely to occur in a single event but can occur through a series of decision-making processes (portfolio and program/project governance) that are undertaken because of inaccurate or incomplete information.
scenario_context.assets: Online retail website Software that facilitate the operation of the online retail website
scenario_context.consequence: Inability to serve customers through an online website
scenario_context.timing: Early detection of the service provider failures and corrective actions are imperative to minimize impact. The time lag between an issue surfacing and being addressed can be short or long, depending on the frequency and effectiveness of program and project status reporting and vendor management.

impact_dimensions.cost_of_response: Incomplete delivery generates the need for further phases or additional project to deliver the complete required outcomes.
impact_dimensions.competitive_advantage: The delay in the business process and I&T operations supported by the service provider can be used by competitors to gain an advantage.
impact_dimensions.reputation: N/A

extents.worst_case: The website stops operating because its software fixes are not received in time and its operation cannot proceed without these critical fixes. The enterprise loses customers because agreed-on service levels are not achieved. The critical IT providers can eventually be replaced, but it will take months to switch to different providers. Customers bring legal actions against the enterprise because it did not meet the agreed-on level of service.
extents.typical_case: The website operates but customers experience some errors, which increases the number of calls to the service center due to customer complaints. This results in high demand for customer service agents to handle complaints. The enterprise loses only a few customers, and the service provider improves its service delivery or can be replaced in a timely manner.
extents.best_case: The website continues to operate, and customers experience only a slow response level in its operation.

11D - Risk Scenario Software License Agr.title: Noncompliance with software license agreements (use and/or distribution of unlicensed software, etc.) occurs resulting in fines and penalties.
11D - Risk Scenario Software License Agr.statement: Legal action is brought by a software provider who identies that the enterprise has violated the software license agreement by unmanaged distribution of the software.
11D - Risk Scenario Software License Agr.oversight: IT Governance Board Architecture Board Steering Committee (programs/projects) Chief Risk Officer (CRO)

scenario_context.intent: Inadvertent, nonmalicious
scenario_context.threat_event: Poor management of software assets
scenario_context.assets: I&T software
scenario_context.consequence: Violation of contractual agreements with software vendor incurs excess costs and creation of a new process for software license management.
scenario_context.timing: Early detection of the project failures and corrective actions are imperative to minimize impact.

impact_dimensions.cost_of_response: Increased costs to initiate a new process to track software assets and manage the procurement and license process. Rework to respond appropriately to the different stakeholders.
impact_dimensions.competitive_advantage: N/A
impact_dimensions.reputation: N/A
impact_dimensions.fines_and_judgements: Legal action is brought by the software provider who identies that the enterprise has violated the software license agreement by unmanaged distribution of the software.

extents.worst_case: The use and mismanagement of software have been occurring for a long period of time. The enterprise must invest significant resources to remedy the problem and initiate a new process for software asset management. No initial agreement is reached with the SAAS vendor or their software vendor. The legal dispute cannot be resolved in the short term and significant fines are levied by the software vendor. The reputation of the enterprise is negatively affected by this situation.
extents.typical_case: An initial agreement is reached with the software provider to inventory and pay for unlicensed software; however, the legal dispute carries a significant financial penalty and investment in new processes to manage software assets.
extents.best_case: An initial agreement is reached with the software provider to inventory and pay for unlicensed software and no fines or judgements are levied against the enterprise from the software enterprise.

mitigating_controls.description: Model and allocate costs. Establish and use an I&T costing model based, for example, on the service definition. This approach ensures that allocation of costs for services is identifiable, measurable and predictable and encourages the responsible use of resources, including those provided by service providers. Regularly review and benchmark the cost/chargeback model to maintain its relevance and appropriateness for evolving business and IT activities.

Manage costs. Implement a cost management process that compares actual costs against budget. Costs should be monitored and reported. Deviations from budget should be identified in a timely manner and their impact on enterprise processes and services assessed.

Identify and record current assets. Maintain an up-to-date, accurate record of all I&T assets that are required to deliver services and that are owned or controlled by the enterprise with an expectation of future benefit (including resources with economic value, such as hardware or software). Ensure alignment with configuration management and financial management.

Manage the asset life cycle. Manage assets from procurement to disposal. Ensure that assets are utilized as effectively and efficiently as possible and are accounted for and physically protected until appropriately retired.

Manage licenses. Manage software licenses to maintain the optimal number of licenses and support business requirements. Ensure that the number of licenses owned is sufficient to cover the installed software in use.

11E - Risk Scenario Inability to Meet Se.statement: Delivery digital services are degraded due to overreliance on a single service provider that cannot scale up to meet increased demand.

scenario_context.intent: The service provider does not have the financial resources to allow it to expand its service capacity to meet the increased demand from its customers.
scenario_context.threat_event: The service provider does not have the financial requirements necessary to obtain financing and be able to grow according to the demand of its customers. Due diligence has not been properly performed by the enterprise procuring the services.
scenario_context.assets: Business processes supported by the service provider Software Systems Databases Infrastructure
scenario_context.consequence: The operation of the business processes supported by the service provider is degraded due to overreliance on this single service provider and this situation brings with it losses of productivity, competitive advantage and reputation.
scenario_context.timing: If the event occurs in a critical period such as the end of the month, it could have a greater impact since it affects even the delivery of time-sensitive processes or financial information to the different stakeholders.

impact_dimensions.cost_of_response: Increased costs to manage performance or possibly replace supplier. Rework to respond appropriately to the different stakeholders.
impact_dimensions.replacement_cost: Scenario may result in incomplete delivery of services and the need for further phases or additional project to deliver the complete outcomes required.
impact_dimensions.competitive_advantage: The delay in the business process and I&T operations supported by the service provider could be used by the competitors to gain an advantage.

12E - Risk Scenario Cross-Boarder Regula.statement: The existence of different regulations between countries prohibits or inhibits technology and information transfer, leading to inability to offer products and services in other countries.

scenario_context.actor: Inexperienced or inadequately trained insiders, contractors and consultants
scenario_context.intent: The threat in this instance is considered inadvertent.
scenario_context.threat_event: The event is unlikely to occur in a single event but can occur through a series of decision-making processes (portfolio and program/project governance) that are made because of inaccurate or incomplete information. Event may also occur where there is a pressure to commence activity before sufficient work has been undertaken to fully clarify and define the requirements for operating in another geographical region.
scenario_context.assets: Business operations
scenario_context.consequence: Complex cross-border regulations can have adverse effect on the enterprise as the business deals with continued regulations, compliance requirements and the cost of changes needed to deliver products and services in other countries.
scenario_context.timing: Monitor when new and changes in regulations are expected to change and the deadlines for effective compliance dates. Take advantage of grace period to adjust to changes when complex regulations are put into effect.

impact_dimensions.cost_of_response: Legal counsel may be needed to implement changes. There may be additional costs and efciency loss due to having to manage differing sets of requirements.
impact_dimensions.competitive_advantage: Local enterprises that do not need to implement cross-border regulations have an advantage.
impact_dimensions.reputation: N/A

extents.worst_case: Enterprise shuts down completely and unable to deliver products and services for 24 weeks. Alternative service and product delivery paths take time to conduct research, investigation and secure new methods of distribution. No technical proficient resources on staff to manage, direct or guide enterprise, so mistakes are made and result in high cost of operations.
extents.typical_case: Enterprise has conducted risk management and has several scenarios for which they have planned responses. There are alternative distribution paths created for products and service delivery options. Technical staff are involved in the planning and the disruption time is minimized. Costs are initially higher than normal but start to stabilize over time. New ways of working strain the staff and some talent is lost but can be replaced in a short time period.
extents.best_case: Enterprise has conducted risk management and has several scenarios for which they have planned responses. There are alternative distribution paths created for products and service delivery options. The situation is of short duration and there is minimal disruption to operations, staff, products and service delivery.

mitigating_controls.description: Evaluate risk management. Continually examine and evaluate the effect of risk on the current and future use of I&T in the enterprise. Consider whether the enterprises risk appetite is appropriate and ensure that risk to enterprise value related to the use of I&T is identified and managed.

Evaluate stakeholder engagement and reporting requirements. Continually examine and evaluate current and future requirements for stakeholder engagement and reporting (including reporting mandated by regulatory requirements), and communication to other stakeholders. Establish principles for engaging and communicating with stakeholders.

Understand enterprise context and direction. Understand the enterprise context (industry drivers, relevant regulations, basis for competition), its current way of working and its ambition level in terms of digitization.

Communicate the I&T strategy and direction. Create awareness and understanding of the business and I&T objectives and direction, as captured in the I&T strategy, through communication to appropriate stakeholders and users throughout the enterprise.

Monitor and scan the technology environment. Set up a technology watch process to perform systematic monitoring and scanning of the enterprises external environment to identify emerging technologies that have the potential to create value (e.g., by realizing the enterprise strategy, optimizing costs, avoiding obsolescence and better enabling enterprise and I&T processes). Monitor the marketplace, competitive landscape, industry sectors, and legal and regulatory trends to be able to analyze emerging technologies or innovation ideas in the enterprise context.

Assess business impact. Identify important services to the enterprise. Map services and resources to business processes and identify business dependencies. Ensure that the impact of unavailable resources is fully agreed on and accepted by the customer. For vital business functions, ensure that availability requirements can be satisfied per service-level agreement.

Perform a feasibility study and formulate alternative solutions. Perform a feasibility study of potential alternative solutions, assess their viability and select the preferred option. If appropriate, implement the selected option as a pilot to determine possible improvements.

Identify external compliance requirements. On a continuous basis, monitor changes in local and international laws, regulations and other external requirements and identify mandates for compliance from an I&T perspective.

Optimize response to external requirements. Review and adjust policies, principles, standards, procedures and methodologies to ensure that legal, regulatory and contractual requirements are addressed and communicated. Consider adopting and adapting industry standards, codes of good practice and good practice guidance.
Confirm external compliance. Confirm compliance of policies, principles, standards, procedures and methodologies with legal, regulatory and contractual requirements.

scenario_context.intent: Cyber-physical threat. Motivated by ideology, religion, social causes or political opinions intended to cause grave harm such as loss of life, or severe economic and organizational damage
scenario_context.threat_event: To adversely affect the enterprises capability and theft of critical intellectual property/asset and sensitive data
scenario_context.assets: The threat actor could misappropriate elements within the facilities, causing damage or theft of critical infrastructure and nationalization of facility operations.
scenario_context.consequence: Any targeted action can affect the system operations and lead to stealing of sensitive data and valuable information and theft of critical documents.
scenario_context.timing: There is no specific time period during which the loss event would not be impactful. The duration of the incident can be very short or prolonged.

impact_dimensions.cost_of_response: The lost intellectual property and product information cannot be recovered in short term.
impact_dimensions.replacement_cost: The attack may leave some components of systems unavailable for use and requires replacement.
impact_dimensions.competitive_advantage: Trust and confidence are eroded leading to reduced organizational value. Advancements in products and new products may be exposed to competitors.
impact_dimensions.reputation: The reputation and goodwill are adversely impacted by loss of ability to continue intended operations.

extents.worst_case: The incident may lead to misuse or unavailability of various IT systems and supply chain leading to long time in recovery and restoration to full operations. Adequate level of maturity in recovery is not achieved due to untested or inadequate planning. The availability of power and network services may also be affected making it difficult to execute BC/DR procedures. Human resources may also be impacted if unavailability of staffing is present in this event. This event may leave the enterprise crippled for days and exposed to various legal issues and long time to recover from products and research information in adversaries' hands.
extents.typical_case: The BCPs (business continuity plans) are executed, but there may be delays in appropriate response due to unavailability of staff and disrupted communications within the disrupted country. Protecting sensitive data and information is made harder by inadequate data management controls and impact is greater than planned in the BCP because of unavailability of staff and power disruptions or public infrastructure failures.
extents.best_case: The RTO/RPO of the system in business continuity may be minimized by adequate monitoring and controls and effective plans in case of any events materialized. The appropriate measures for protecting sensitive data and information are protected by data management controls and impact is minimal due to prior notice to plan.

During such incidences of operations use alternative data center and telecom facility as per BCP (business continuity plan) will be required. scenario_context.intent: N/A
scenario_context.threat_event: The threat is complex and can be caused by many factors, including: Increase in opportunity and operational cost against industry index Loss of market share due to new products and services not meeting expectations Losing advantage to competitors because product is not meeting business needs or not achieving targeted benefits discussed in business case. Inadequate automation in products and services for long-impact goodwill Gap in skills and competency of staff
scenario_context.assets: Products and services portfolio, new innovative products
scenario_context.consequence: Productivity has not improved in line with the industry trend. Cost of response may become high in terms of opportunity loss, due to product low performance. Competitive advantage is lost to competitors, resulting in market share loss.
scenario_context.timing: The duration of change in processes and functionality can be a longer time than expected and can incur continuous strain due to ineffective and inefficient delivery of envisaged new services. However, the service-level impact improves business competency in meeting the expectations of customers. Dependence on traditional methods and legacy products remains, and their inefficient services impact customer morale negatively. The adverse response to the change to new technology endures for a long time, while the system is being set to the desired level.

impact_dimensions.cost_of_response: Cost increases with time due to inadequate number of skilled and competent staff and benefits not available.
impact_dimensions.competitive_advantage: Competitive advantage is lost due to delay in delivery of new tech-based products and services.
impact_dimensions.reputation: Reputation suffers due to delay in delivery of new tech-based products and service.

extents.worst_case: Optimizing the use of technology by adopting emerging technology to meet the business requirements may affect profitability adversely, while the industry trend of adopting new technology grows with time. The loss of market share, reputation and advantages cannot be recovered in the short run.
extents.typical_case: IT adopts the strategy to evaluate and assess products and services to align them with the business by changing processes and functions to match those envisaged in the business plan. This strategy can deliver value after the changes are made. Change management of the implementation process and functions development and testing leads to delivery of expected benefits.
extents.best_case: Addressing concerns about deviation from enterprise goals and targets helps with planning and organizing implementation and delivers results quicker. Fast expected results are delivered when business stakeholders participate in process and functional architectural change reviews, communication and practices are effective, priority order is adopted, and competent resources are used.

mitigating_controls.description: EDM02.02 Evaluate value optimization by new technology product and services. Continually evaluate the portfolio of I&T-enabled investments, services and assets to determine the likelihood of achieving enterprise objectives and delivering value. APO02.01 Understand enterprise context and direction. Understand the enterprise context (industry drivers, relevant regulations, basis for competition), its current way of working and its ambition level in terms of digitization.

APO02.03 Define target digital capabilities in context of adopted new technology. Based on the understanding of enterprise context and direction, define the target I&T products and services and required capabilities. Consider reference standards, best practices and validated emerging technologies.

APO02.05 Define the strategic plan and road map. Develop a holistic digital strategy, in cooperation with relevant stakeholders, and detail a road map that defines the incremental steps required to achieve the goals and objectives. Ensure focus on the transformation journey through the appointment of a person who helps spearhead the digital transformation and drives alignment between business and I&T.

APO02.06 Communicate the I&T strategy and direction about changes by new technology. Create awareness and understanding of the business and I&T objectives and direction, as captured in the I&T strategy, through communication to appropriate stakeholders and users throughout the enterprise.

APO03.01 Develop the enterprise architecture vision to optimize value of new technology. The architecture vision provides a first-cut, high-level description of the baseline and target architectures, covering the business, information, data, application and technology domains. The architecture vision provides the sponsor with a key tool to sell the benefits of the proposed capabilities to stakeholders within the enterprise. The architecture vision describes how the new capabilities (in line with I&T strategy and objectives) will meet enterprise goals and strategic objectives and address stakeholder concerns when implemented.

APO03.03 Select opportunities and solution by use of new technology as envisaged. Rationalize the gaps between baseline and target architectures, accounting for both business and technical perspectives, and logically group them into project work packages. Integrate the project with any related I&T-enabled investment programs to ensure that the architectural initiatives are aligned with and enable these initiatives as part of overall enterprise change. Make this a collaborative effort with key enterprise stakeholders from business and IT to assess the enterprise's transformation readiness, and identify opportunities, solutions and all implementation constraints.

APO04.01 Create an environment conducive to innovation in use of new technology. Create an environment that is conducive to innovation, considering methods such as culture, reward, collaboration, technology forums, and mechanisms to promote and capture employee ideas.

APO04.04 Assess the potential of emerging technologies and innovative ideas. Analyze identified emerging technologies and/or other I&T innovative suggestions to understand their business potential. Work with stakeholders to validate assumptions on the potential of new technologies and innovation.

extents.best_case: The enterprise misses the opportunity to be more sustainable. No warning or fine is received.

scenario_context.intent: Information theft
scenario_context.threat_event: Sensitive information and data are emailed from the enterprise email to the personal email account of a person leaving the firm, taking with them key customer information and contacts.
scenario_context.assets: High-value customer data
scenario_context.consequence: The enterprise loses IP and/or suffers leakage of competitive information.
scenario_context.timing: The duration depends on how promptly the missing information is discovered. Early detection minimizes the impact and is key to limit the scope of the customers affected.

impact_dimensions.cost_of_response: Investigation of what data and how much data are missing takes time and resources to clean up and put in place new procedures to prevent recurrence of incident.
impact_dimensions.replacement_cost: Loss of key customers and the expenditure of resources to regain previous customers or seek new customers
impact_dimensions.competitive_advantage: Competitors take advantage of leaked info. Customer info allowed new enterprise to gain advantage due to insider information.
impact_dimensions.reputation: N/A

extents.worst_case: Data loss is of the complete customer records. Data loss is undetected for a long period of time resulting in serious customer churn and significant percentage of lost customers. Customer records contain sensitive information which violates privacy regulations resulting in fines and reputational losses.
extents.typical_case: An unknown amount of customer data is lost. Discovery of incident takes weeks. Incident response teams are unable to determine the amount and full scope of the data loss. Rework ensues to recreate or appropriately mark existing critical or high-value data and put procedures in place to prevent another incident.
extents.best_case: Email detection is in place and the email is recalled before leaving the enterprise. Only a small portion of data was lost and is quickly recovered. Customers are contacted promptly and a resolution is provided to minimize impact.

Ensure a data quality assessment approach. Provide a systematic approach to measure and evaluate data quality according to processes and techniques, and against data quality rules.

Identify and classify sources of information for governance and management of I&T. Identify, validate and classify diverse sources of internal and external information required to enable governance and management of I&T, including strategy documents, incident reports and configuration information that progresses from development to operations before going live.

Organize and contextualize information into knowledge. Organize information based on classification criteria. Identify and create meaningful relationships among information elements and enable use of information. Identify owners, and leverage and implement enterprise-defined information levels of access to management information and knowledge resources.

scenario_context.assets: Data and information
scenario_context.consequence: Increase in customer service calls, budget overruns for customer service staff overtime and inability to locate high-value or critical business process information when needed
scenario_context.timing: The duration depends on how promptly the inaccurate or missing information is discovered and corrected. Prevention of incorrect data entry and early detection errors minimizes the impact on the timeline.

impact_dimensions.cost_of_response: Continuously answering calls, staff burnout, lost revenue or reputation from lost customers
impact_dimensions.replacement_cost: Data and information that is corrupted or unable to be located must be recreated to continue to service the customers

extents.typical_case: Angry customers, excessive rework, staff burnout, increased budget due to overtime and lost productivity

Manage errors and exceptions. Manage business process exceptions and errors and facilitate remediation, executing defined corrective actions and escalating as necessary. This treatment of exceptions and errors provides assurance of the accuracy and integrity of the business information process.

Ensure traceability and accountability for information events. Ensure that business information can be traced to an originating business event and associated with accountable parties. This discoverability provides assurance that business information is reliable and has been processed in accordance with defined objectives.

1A - Risk Scenario Misaligned Programs.d.statement: Programs selected for implementation are misaligned with corporate strategy and priorities, resulting in an inappropriate new CRM (customer relationship management) application that fails to support the customer service strategy

scenario_context.actor: The scenario is not malicious in nature and would be inadvertently caused by enterprise insider(s)
scenario_context.intent: Unintentional event resulting from inadequate requirements, planning, execution or oversight by enterprise insider(s)
scenario_context.threat_event: Event is considered inadvertent. Event may occur when: There is insufficient clarity and granularity as to corporate strategy and priorities, in this case in relation to the appropriate requirements for customer relations management) (CRM) Customer service strategy is not sufficiently well defined or not sufficiently understood by all stakeholders in portfolio decision making CRM application functionality and features are not well enough understood to ensure that they meet the strategic CRM requirements. The event is unlikely to occur in a single event but can occur through a series of decision-making processes (portfolio and program/project governance) that are made because of inaccurate or incomplete information Pressure to commence activity before sufficient work has been undertaken to fully clarify the strategy and priorities and define the required outcomes and the intermediate delivery stages to reach those desired outcomes
scenario_context.assets: The asset under threat is the achievement of strategy, and in this scenario, the strategy and capability relating to CRM and the associated customer service activities
scenario_context.consequence: Enterprise is not able to deliver its customer service strategy and does not have sufficient remaining capital to deliver it within acceptable timescale. There is likely to be both a tangible impact to this (delivery of organizational capability/service/capacity) and an intangible impact (improved reputation due to better products, better customer service, etc.)
scenario_context.timing: Early detection of the project failures and corrective actions are imperative to minimize impact. The scenario assumes the new CRM application has been implemented; thus, the scenario is most impactful to consider at the beginning of project initiation The misalignment of strategic objectives to solution should be identified through relevant rigor employed at all key program and project stage gates, and specifically those at project commencement that confirm the required outcomes and their alignment to strategy and strategic priorities The time lag between an issue surfacing and being addressed could be short or long, depending on the frequency and effectiveness of program and project status reporting

impact_dimensions.cost_of_response: N/A
impact_dimensions.replacement_cost: If the overall strategy and CRM strategy remain valid, then a further investment is required to deliver functionality to correctly support the CRM strategy
impact_dimensions.competitive_advantage: If the CRM strategy had been communicated or advertised externally and would have provided competitive advantage, then any failure to deliver the required strategic outcomes impacts the expected advantage to be gained
impact_dimensions.reputation: If the CRM strategy had been communicated or advertised externally, then any failure to deliver the required strategic outcomes impacts market and customer sentiment and hence reputation
impact_dimensions.fines_and_judgements: A CRM strategy delivery is unlikely to have any regulatory or legal delivery requirement; however, if the lack of functionality in the CRM delivery resulted in customer privacy detrimental impacts, this may prompt regulatory sanctions

extents.worst_case: New CRM application cannot support any element of the required customer service strategy and must be decommissioned without addressing any corporate strategies
extents.typical_case: New CRM application requires substantial investment or customization to achieve elements of the required customer service strategy but cannot on its own provide all the outcomes required even with additional investment
extents.best_case: New CRM application can be customized and enhanced with minimal effort and cost to achieve the required customer service strategy

scenario_context.actor: Inexperienced or inadequately trained project staff. The threat in this instance is considered inadvertent
scenario_context.intent: Unintentional event resulting from untrained staff, inadequate training requirements, planning, execution or oversight by enterprise insider(s)
scenario_context.threat_event: Event is considered inadvertent. Event may occur when: There is insufficient clarity and granularity as to the precise outcome and deliverables required of the program in relation to investment funds available functionality within the accounting system to enable the broader customer outcome required There is insufficient funding allocated to the program to deliver all the required functionality within the new accounting system New accounting system functionality and features are not well enough understood to ensure that they meet the investment funds selection criteria required as an outcome for the customer-facing application Insufficient understanding of integration requirements between new accounting system and customer-facing application to ensure end-to-end outcomes can be achieved The event is unlikely to occur in a single event but can occur through a series of decision-making processes (portfolio and program/project governance) that are made because of inaccurate or incomplete information Event may also occur where there is a pressure to commence activity before sufficient work has been undertaken to fully clarify and define the required outcomes for both the new accounting system and the overall end-to-end customer-facing application
scenario_context.assets: The asset is the ultimate project or program deliverable in relation to both the new accounting system and the customer-facing application which it supports. There is likely to be both a tangible aspect to this (delivery of organizational capability/service/capacity) and an intangible aspect (improved reputation due to better products, better customer service, etc.)
scenario_context.consequence: Multichannel customer-facing application is unable to provide the planned/expected choice of investment funds and may not have sufficient capital available to deliver the full functionality within acceptable timescales
scenario_context.timing: Early detection of the project failures and corrective actions are imperative to minimize impact. The scenario assumes the new accounting system has been implemented; thus, the scenario is most impactful to consider at the beginning of project initiation The misalignment of strategic objectives to accounting system functionality solution should be identified through relevant rigor employed at all key program and project stage gates, and specifically those at project commencement that confirm the required outcomes for the new accounting system and the alignment of these to the broader customer-facing application which it supports The time lag between an issue surfacing and being addressed could be short or long, depending on the frequency and effectiveness of program and project status reporting

impact_dimensions.reputation: If the multichannel customer-facing application and its funds choice options had been communicated or marketed externally, then failure to deliver impacts the reputation

extents.best_case: New accounting system can be amended or reconfigured at minimal cost/time to provide the required investment funds choice options required by the customer-facing application

scenario_context.threat_event: The threat is considered inadvertent Some causes are: Insufficient clarity of requirements as to the precise skills and capabilities required to implement and support new infrastructure Lack of understanding of the precise capability of the cloud infrastructure required to achieve the intended outcomes or meet requirements Lack of knowledge or understanding of new infrastructure limitations or restrictions Lack of testing of infrastructure prior to full implementation or confirmation of operation through proof of concept Precise capabilities of the selected cloud infrastructure are not fully compatible or available to meet requirements The event is unlikely to occur in a single event but can occur through a series of decision-making processes (portfolio and program/project governance) that are made based on inaccurate or incomplete information with respect to staff skills and experience, and infrastructure solution availability and capability. scenario_context.assets: The asset is the delivery of the new infrastructure

scenario_context.intent: Event is considered inadvertent. scenario_context.threat_event: The event is unlikely to occur in a single event but can occur through a series of decision-making processes (portfolio and program/project governance) that are made because of inaccurate or incomplete information, poor communication and lack of project coordination Event may also occur where there is a pressure to commence activity before sufficient work has been undertaken to fully clarify the strategy and priorities and define the required outcomes and the solutions to achieve those desired outcomes
scenario_context.assets: The asset is the financial investment and IT operating budget for the enterprise
scenario_context.consequence: Portfolio investment is duplicated on multiple customer databases and not available for other programs. IT operating costs increase due to duplicate customer databases. Customer servicing may be impacted if databases are not aligned or hold different or conflicting information
scenario_context.timing: The scale and impact of the scenario depends on how early in the planning or development of the project the potential duplication of customer databases is identified. scenario_context.threat_event: Event is considered inadvertent. Event may occur when: There is insufficient clarity and granularity as to the precise outcome and deliverables required of the program in relation to strategic I&T investment. There is insufficient funding allocated to the program to deliver all the required functionality Limitation of enterprise architecture for developing complete functionalities and providing resilience and scalability for expansion Insufficient understanding of integration requirements between new I&T and existing architecture The event is unlikely to occur in a single event but can occur through a series of decision-making processes (portfolio and program/project governance) that are made because of inaccurate or incomplete information. Event may also occur where there is a pressure to commence activity before sufficient work has been undertaken to fully clarify and define the required outcomes.

Assess current digital maturity of the enterprise and its appetite for change.

Develop the enterprise architecture vision. The architecture vision provides a first-cut, high-level description of the baseline and target architectures, covering the business, information, data, application and technology domains. The architecture vision describes how the new capabilities (in line with I&T strategy and objectives) meet enterprise goals and strategic objectives and address stakeholder concerns when implemented.
Define reference architecture. The reference architecture describes the current and target architectures for the business, information, data, application and technology domains.

Select opportunities and solutions from changes in enterprise architecture. Rationalize the gaps between baseline and target architectures, accounting for both business and technical perspectives, and logically group them into project work packages. Integrate the project with any related I&T-enabled investment programs to ensure that the architectural initiatives are aligned with and enable these initiatives as part of overall enterprise change. Make this a collaborative effort with key enterprise stakeholders from business and IT to assess the enterprise's transformation readiness and identify opportunities, solutions and all implementation constraints for change of enterprise architecture.

Provide enterprise architecture services. Provide enterprise architecture services within the enterprise that include guidance to and monitoring of implementation projects, formalizing ways of working through architecture contracts and measuring and communicating architectures value and compliance monitoring.
