extents.best_case: The enterprise maintains details of all architectural changes and it makes necessary changes in architecture repository information to detect duplicate. As records of all components are available, the enterprise resolves issues of governance of enterprise architecture with least costs.

mitigating_controls.description: Establish the target investment mix. Review and ensure clarity of the enterprise and I&T strategies and current services. Define an appropriate investment mix based on cost, alignment with strategy, type of benefit for the programs in the portfolio, degree of risk and financial measures such as cost and expected ROI (return on investment) over the full economic life cycle. Adjust the enterprise and I&T strategies where necessary.
Define reference architecture. The reference architecture describes the current and target architectures for the business, information, data, application and technology domains.

Define architecture implementation. Create a viable implementation and migration plan in alignment with the program and project portfolios. Ensure the plan is closely coordinated to deliver value and that the required resources are available to complete the necessary work.

Maintain a standard approach for program management. Maintain a standard approach for program management that enables governance and management review, decision making and delivery-management activities. These activities should focus consistently on business value and goals (i.e., requirements, risk, costs, schedule and quality targets).

Define and maintain business functional and technical requirements. Based on the business case, identify, prioritize, specify and agree on business information, functional, technical and control requirements covering the scope/understanding of all initiatives required to achieve the expected outcomes of the proposed I&T-enabled business solution.

key_risk_indicators.description: Date of the last update to domain and/or federated architectures
Number of exceptions to architecture standards and baselines applied for and granted
Percentage of successful programs based on the defined standard approach
Percentage of stakeholders satisfied with architecture program management
Percentage of requirements reworked due to misalignment with enterprise needs and expectations
Clear definition of architecture implementation governance requirements
Percentage of stakeholders aware of architecture implementation and migration

5F Risk Scenario Excessive-Number-of-Exc.title: There are excessive number of exceptions to following existing enterprise architecture standards.
5F Risk Scenario Excessive-Number-of-Exc.statement: In the past 12 months, almost 75 percentage of the new projects have requested (and been granted) exceptions to the enterprise architecture standards resulting in inconsistent solutions, increased complexity of the environment and excessive costs.
5F Risk Scenario Excessive-Number-of-Exc.oversight: I&T Governance Board Steering Committee (programs/projects) Architecture Board

scenario_context.actor: IT project management process ignoring compliance to enterprise architecture
scenario_context.intent: Intentional event resulting from inadequate attention to enterprise architecture design requirements, planning, execution or oversight by enterprise insider(s) Excessive violations of enterprise architecture standard due to siloed decision making
scenario_context.threat_event: Creating limitations of integration of enterprise architecture by exceptions resulting in additional costs and degradation of IT performance (threat to architectural governance)
scenario_context.assets: The Architectural Assets, Reference Architecture Framework, Artifacts and Building Blocks (Patterns, Components and Components Library), Technology Architecture, Information System Architecture and Security Architecture
scenario_context.consequence: The exceptions in enterprise architecture lead to inconsistencies of architecture and result in extra cost for removal of exceptions that cause alignment issues.
scenario_context.timing: It is generally undesirable timing to allow exceptions when there is high demand for I&T services. The architecture reviews must be held at appropriate project milestones or checkpoints in the projects life cycle, at a stage when there is still time to correct any major errors or shortcomings.

impact_dimensions.cost_of_response: The costs are multiplied to manage target enterprise architecture as the sunk costs and rework costs are added.
impact_dimensions.replacement_cost: The obsolescence of applications and solutions and artifacts, patterns and services which are replaced in compliance with the target enterprise architecture
impact_dimensions.competitive_advantage: Competitors increase due to slower delivery of products and services to meet customer needs.
impact_dimensions.reputation: The reputation is impacted due to the slow performance and incomplete functionalities of the I&T architecture.

extents.worst_case: The enterprise continuously fails to meet customer obligations due to complex, proprietary architecture that is unable to provide new functionalities and capacity of the required scale to deliver I&T projects on time and budget. The enterprise loses market share and customers and thus leads to revenue and profitability loss.
extents.typical_case: The enterprise discourages exceptions in its policy but continues to allow them in practice. The time involved to close the gaps and review the appropriate documentation to align with target architecture is not a priority. The enterprise faces problems in the continued one-off changes in architecture and is unable to achieve stability. This instability causes incompatible I&T solutions and incurs excess cost and inconvenience to stakeholders.
extents.best_case: The enterprise maintains integrity of target enterprise architecture and any exceptions are for temporary duration. The enterprise architecture assets are appropriately managed to reconcile with the standard architecture. An agile approach is maintained to achieve the efficiency and effectiveness in compliance with target architecture.

mitigating_controls.description: Evaluate value optimization. Continually evaluate the portfolio of I&T-enabled investments, services and assets to determine the likelihood of achieving enterprise objectives and delivering value. Identify and evaluate any changes in direction to management that optimize value creation.

Develop the enterprise architecture vision. The architecture vision provides a first-cut, high-level description of the baseline and target architectures, covering the business, information, data, application and technology domains. The architecture vision provides the sponsor with a key tool to sell the benefits of the proposed capabilities to stakeholders within the enterprise. The architecture vision describes how the new capabilities (in line with I&T strategy and objectives) meet enterprise goals and strategic objectives and address stakeholder concerns when implemented.
Define reference architecture. The reference architecture describes the current and target architectures for the business, information, data, application and technology domains.

Perform quality monitoring, control and reviews. Monitor the quality of processes and services on an ongoing basis, in line with quality management standards. Define, plan and implement measurements to monitor customer satisfaction with quality and the value provided by the QMS (quality management system). The information gathered should be used by the process owner to improve quality.

Perform QA (quality assurance). Develop, resource and execute a QA plan aligned with the QMS to obtain the quality specified in the requirements definition and in the enterprises quality policies and procedures.
Establish and maintain a configuration repository and baseline. Establish and maintain a configuration management repository and create controlled configuration baselines.

Manage errors and exceptions. Manage business process exceptions and errors and facilitate remediation, executing defined corrective actions and escalating as necessary. This treatment of exceptions and errors provides assurance of the accuracy and integrity of the business information processes.

Percentage of portfolio of I&T-enabled investments with a likelihood of achieving enterprise objectives and delivering value at a reasonable cost
Degree to which the baseline and target architectures cover the business, information, data, application and technology domains and frequency of updates
Percentage of accuracy of configuration baselines of a service, application or infrastructure
Percentage of projects reviewed that meet target quality goals and objectives

6A Risk Scenario Mistakes-Made-During-Up.title: Mistakes, errors and omissions are made by IT staff during backup, during upgrades of systems, during maintenance of systems, etc.
6A Risk Scenario Mistakes-Made-During-Up.statement: IT operations staff (internal or at the service provider) enters incorrect information during an upgrade of a system, leaving out critical security configuration steps, which increases the susceptibility of the I&T systems to risk.
6A Risk Scenario Mistakes-Made-During-Up.oversight: I&T Governance Board Human Resources Steering Committee (programs /projects) Chief Risk Officer

scenario_context.actor: The scenario is not malicious in nature and would be caused by enterprise insider(s). It is a deliberate activity and therefore cannot be considered inadvertent or accidental.
scenario_context.intent: The event is due to an enterprise insider and is deliberate but not malicious. The event may be caused by: Lack of understanding of enterprise approach and process to identifying, prioritizing and delivering IT-related changes Lack of knowledge of requirements in respect of current enterprise processes Lack of training or awareness of the correct procedures May be in a rush to get work done, or unfamiliar, untrained, may be tired, disengaged, etc.
scenario_context.threat_event: The event may occur in a single event and can also occur through a series of decision-making processes which occur both inside the I&T projects and within the relevant business department.
scenario_context.assets: All I&T systems & data
scenario_context.consequence: Increased exposure to risk due to insecure configuration. For example, this may result in unintentionally leaving a port open on a web server, thus increasing its ability to be discovered by a malicious actor.
scenario_context.timing: Any I&T interruption during busy season or when transactions or financial deadlines are at a high volume may negatively impact important I&T systems. Off-season event impact may be less severe.

impact_dimensions.cost_of_response: Overall response costs can be higher as teams need to respond to mistakes and delays in operations. Project teams may also not be trained, leading to continued mistakes, errors and omissions that overrun the budget, leaving little money for training.
impact_dimensions.competitive_advantage: Security technology does not operate properly because of insufficient IT staff skills and knowledge. The enterprise might lose a competitive advantage if they are focused on rework and clean-up of mistakes.
impact_dimensions.reputation: Loss of trust in I&T staff because of continued mistakes impacts their reputation internally and externally.

extents.worst_case: Depending on the severity of the mistake, error or omission of critical security configuration settings, there may be widespread damage to various IT systems and supply chain leading to a long time to recover and restore operations. Adequate level of maturity in recovery is not achieved due to untested or inadequate planning.
extents.typical_case: The enterprise has procedures, but maintenance has not occurred for some time. This results in delays and excess downtime to restore services to their operational state. The systems slowly become operational as procedures are learned and implemented. Data integrity issues may also lead to delays in operational effectiveness. There may be a series of near misses which makes management take the appropriate action before a serious event occurs. Rework costs are high when mistakes are prevalent.
extents.best_case: A series of near misses makes management take the appropriate action before a serious event occurs. Management introduces training, common document repository and assigns responsibility for updating procedures.

mitigating_controls.description: Direct stakeholder engagement, communication and reporting. Ensure the establishment of effective stakeholder involvement, communication and reporting, including mechanisms for ensuring the quality and completeness of information, overseeing mandatory reporting and creating a communication strategy for stakeholders.

Communicate management objectives, direction and decisions made. Communicate awareness and promote understanding of alignment and I&T objectives to stakeholders throughout the enterprise. Communicate at regular intervals on important I&T-related decisions and their impact for the enterprise.

Define and communicate policies and procedures. Put in place procedures to maintain compliance with and performance measurement of policies and other components of the control framework. Enforce the consequences of noncompliance or inadequate performance. Track trends and performance and consider these in the future design and improvement of the control framework.

Maintain the skills and competencies of personnel. Define and manage the skills and competencies required of personnel. Regularly verify that personnel have the competencies to fulfill their roles on the basis of their education, training and/or experience. Verify that these competencies are being maintained, using qualification and certification programs where appropriate. Provide employees with ongoing learning and opportunities to maintain their knowledge, skills and competencies at a level required to achieve enterprise goals.

Assess and recognize/reward employee job performance. Conduct timely, regular performance evaluations against individual objectives derived from enterprise goals, established standards, specific job responsibilities, and the skills and competency framework. Implement a remuneration/recognition process that rewards successful attainment of performance goals.

Manage quality standards, practices and procedures and integrate quality management into key processes and solutions. Identify and maintain standards, procedures and practices for key processes to guide the enterprise in meeting the intent of the agreed quality management standards. This activity should align with I&T control framework requirements. Consider certification for key processes, organizational units, products or services.

Number of processes with defined quality requirements
Number of SLAs that include quality acceptance criteria

6B Risk Scenario Incorrect-Input-of-Info.title: Incorrect information is input by IT staff or system users.
6B Risk Scenario Incorrect-Input-of-Info.statement: The system manager of a critical server enters incorrect network information into the system, crippling the communication speed of the system to unacceptable levels, or a system user inputs incorrect parameters which can lead to errors in calculation or data processing.
6B Risk Scenario Incorrect-Input-of-Info.oversight: I&T Governance Board Human Resources Steering Committee (programs/projects) Chief Risk Officer

6D_Risk Scenario Inadequate-Patch-Vulner.title: Patch/vulnerability management process is inadequate to prevent incidents
6D_Risk Scenario Inadequate-Patch-Vulner.statement: Inadequate patch and vulnerability management leaves systems vulnerable to attacks or crashes, reducing service levels.
6D_Risk Scenario Inadequate-Patch-Vulner.oversight: I&T Governance Board Architecture Review Board Steering Committee (Programs/ Projects) Chief Risk Officer

scenario_context.intent: N/A
scenario_context.threat_event: The event may occur in a single event and can also occur through a series of decision-making processes, which occur inside the I&T projects and within the relevant business department.
scenario_context.assets: All I&T systems
scenario_context.consequence: Increased exposure to risk due to poor coverage and implementation of patching processes
scenario_context.timing: Incident can be severe if it takes place during a mission-critical business period.

impact_dimensions.cost_of_response: Response costs are payroll costs for incident responders, communications, PR, management meetings, forensics, etc., during an incident due to the exploited vulnerability.
impact_dimensions.replacement_cost: If the vulnerability exploitation causes severe damage to the system, replacement costs may be needed.
impact_dimensions.competitive_advantage: Competitive advantage may be impacted by significant productivity loss and reputation harm.
impact_dimensions.reputation: If the incident affects a customer-facing service for a significant time period, the organization reputation is negatively impacted.

extents.worst_case: Vulnerability of a customer-facing server is exploited, resulting in: Website deface and service unavailability Lateral movement into organization internal network successfully obtains Super User privileges (e.g., domain administrator account) Leaked organization data, including confidential and personal data
extents.typical_case: Vulnerability exploitation results in service unavailability or website deface. Recovery procedures are in place and restoration is possible. Cost of clean-up and productivity losses occur due to website availability.
extents.best_case: Vulnerability exploitation results in providing read-only access to the attacker in a website folder tree that does not include confidential or personal data.

6E Risk Scenario Inadequate-Performance-.title: Performance and operations monitoring is inadequate to detect problems before they materialize.
6E Risk Scenario Inadequate-Performance-.statement: Inadequate systems or application monitoring can cause system capacity or availability degradation to remain unnoticed for too long, leading to service interruptions.
6E Risk Scenario Inadequate-Performance-.oversight: I&T Governance Board Architecture Review Board Steering Committee (programs/projects) Chief Risk Officer

scenario_context.intent: The event is due to an enterprise insider and is deliberate but not malicious. The event may be caused by: Lack of understanding of enterprise approach and process for monitoring Lack of monitoring tools, techniques or methods Lack of training or awareness of the value of the monitoring process
scenario_context.threat_event: The event may occur in a single event and can also occur through a series of decision-making processes which occur both inside the I&T projects and within the relevant business department.
scenario_context.assets: All I&T assets and systems
scenario_context.consequence: Inability to have visibility into problems or risk before it materializes into an incident
scenario_context.timing: The misalignment of I&T strategies and planning for monitoring should be identified through key program and project stage gates, and specifically those at project commencement that confirm the required outcomes for the I&T systems on which the enterprise relies. The time lag between an issue surfacing and being addressed could be short or long, depending on the frequency and effectiveness of program planning, business impact analysis and awareness of risk.

impact_dimensions.cost_of_response: Incident clean-up costs rather than proactive monitoring budget
impact_dimensions.competitive_advantage: N/A
impact_dimensions.reputation: Reputation is diminished due to unavailability of the services that the enterprise is obligated to deliver but is unable to deliver.
impact_dimensions.fines_and_judgements: SLA breaches may also be imposed.

extents.worst_case: Extended delays in responding to events or failure to respond to a security event in a timely manner due to lack of monitoring. The security event may be an undetected data breach or exfiltration that results in a serious financial impact.
extents.typical_case: Delays in responding to events or resolving project- or product-level issues/bug due to lack of monitoring. Inability to have visibility into capacity and availability increases failures that may have been prevented. This can result in unintended inefficiencies, lower productivity and increased costs from rework.
extents.best_case: Several near misses in responding to events and potential failures happen. Inability to have visibility into capacity and availability is understood to be an issue that needs a resolution before a serious event occurs.

mitigating_controls.description: Monitor the governance system. Monitor the effectiveness and performance of the enterprises governance of I&T. Assess whether the governance system and implemented mechanisms (including structures, principles and processes) are operating effectively and provide appropriate oversight of I&T to enable value creation.
Monitor risk management. Monitor the key goals and metrics of the risk management processes. Determine how deviations or problems are identified, tracked and reported for remediation.

Set up a technology watch process to perform systematic monitoring and scanning of the enterprises external environment to identify emerging technologies that have the potential to create value (e.g., by realizing the enterprise strategy, optimizing costs, avoiding obsolescence and better enabling enterprise and I&T processes). Monitor the marketplace, competitive landscape, industry sectors, and legal and regulatory trends to be able to analyze emerging technologies or innovation ideas in the enterprise context.
Monitor and report service levels. Monitor service levels, report on achievements and identify trends. Provide the appropriate management information to aid performance management.

Define, plan and implement measurements to monitor customer satisfaction with quality and the value provided by the QMS. The information gathered should be used by the process owner to improve quality.

6F Risk Scenario Inadequate-Facility-Res.title: Facility resilience is inadequate to protect and sustain all I&T asset types.
6F Risk Scenario Inadequate-Facility-Res.statement: Poor maintenance and planning for continuity, disasters and incidents leave the enterprise exposed to conditions that impact its ability to maintain resilience.
6F Risk Scenario Inadequate-Facility-Res.oversight: I&T Governance Board Architecture Review Board Steering Committee (programs/projects) Chief Risk Officer

scenario_context.intent: Unintentional event resulting from inadequate scenario planning for incidents, risks and conditions that would prevent the enterprise from maintaining resilience for I&T assets
scenario_context.threat_event: Poor planning for business resilience
scenario_context.assets: All I&T assets
scenario_context.consequence: The primary consequence here is unavailability of I&T systems, information and assets
scenario_context.timing: The misalignment of I&T strategies and business resilience planning should be identified through key program and project stage gates, and specifically those at project commencement that confirm the required outcomes for the I&T systems on which the enterprise relies. The time lag between an issue surfacing and being addressed could be short or long, depending on the frequency and effectiveness of program planning, business impact analysis and awareness of risk.

impact_dimensions.cost_of_response: Response costs may include rework to restore lost data and information, repair or replace I&T equipment or hire new staff or vendors to deliver services and products.
impact_dimensions.replacement_cost: Depending on the type of event, there may be significant replacement costs to procure I&T assets that have not been sufficiently maintained or protected.
impact_dimensions.competitive_advantage: Enterprise loses competitive advantage if they are no longer providing service to customers.
impact_dimensions.reputation: Reputation is diminished due to unavailability of the services that the enterprise delivers.

extents.worst_case: Entire production environment could become unavailable due to power outage or any other natural disaster. The recovery and restoration period would be extended if poor resilience planning occurred.
extents.typical_case: One or more large and/or time critical unavailability events happen and make management take the appropriate action before a more serious event occurs. Management introduces training, awareness of the need for resilience and assigns responsibility for updating resilience planning procedures.
extents.best_case: A series of small unavailability events happens and makes management take the appropriate action before a serious event occurs. Management introduces training, awareness of the need for resilience and assigns responsibility for updating resilience planning procedures.

mitigating_controls.description: Direct risk management. Direct the establishment of risk management practices to provide reasonable assurance that I&T risk management practices are appropriate and that actual I&T risk does not exceed the boards risk appetite.

Communicate management objectives, direction and decisions made. Communicate awareness and promote understanding of alignment and I&T objectives to stakeholders throughout the enterprise. Communicate at regular intervals on important I&T-related decisions and their impact for the enterprise.

Define and communicate policies and procedures. Put in place procedures to maintain compliance with and performance measurement of policies and other components of the control framework. Enforce the consequences of noncompliance or inadequate performance. Track trends and performance and consider these in the future design and improvement of the control framework.
Manage data backup and restore arrangements. Manage availability of critical data to ensure operational continuity.

Assess business impact. Identify important services to the enterprise. Map services and resources to business processes and identify business dependencies. Ensure that the impact of unavailable resources is fully agreed on and accepted by the customer. For vital business functions, ensure that availability requirements can be satisfied per service-level agreement
Manage critical assets. Identify assets that are critical in providing service capability. Maximize their reliability and availability to support business needs.
Define the business continuity policy, objectives and scope. Define business continuity policy and scope, aligned with enterprise and stakeholder objectives, to improve business resilience.

Maintain business resilience. Evaluate business resilience options and choose a cost-effective and viable strategy that ensures enterprise continuity, disaster recovery and incident response in the face of a disaster or other major incident or disruption.

7A Risk Scenario Compromised-Software-In.title: Software integrity is compromised through inadvertent or malicious means.
7A Risk Scenario Compromised-Software-In.statement: Authorized users with access to information resources unintentionally or maliciously affect the confidentiality, integrity or availability of systems, causing a security incident.
7A Risk Scenario Compromised-Software-In.oversight: I&T Governance Board Chief Risk Officer (CRO)

scenario_context.intent: The event can be caused unintentionally or maliciously by organizational insiders. Motivations of nonmalicious insiders can be benign, while the motives of malicious insiders can be financial gain, vandalism or other forms of criminal activity.
scenario_context.threat_event: Software integrity is compromised by the actions of an insider
scenario_context.assets: Entire IT operation systems
scenario_context.consequence: Security incidents, including data disclosure, tampering and outages
scenario_context.timing: The duration of the incident can be very short or prolonged, depending on job scope and overlap of duties. Early detection and corrective action are key to limit the scope and nature of this risk scenario.

impact_dimensions.cost_of_response: Time/efforts to identify root causes and recover from an incident
impact_dimensions.competitive_advantage: N/A
impact_dimensions.reputation: If the events are severe enough and public facing, an enterprises reputation can adversely be impacted due to nonavailability and delays.
impact_dimensions.fines_and_judgements: If the events are severe enough and public facing, exposure to fines and regulatory and legal compliances are possible.

extents.worst_case: Security and outage incidents can result in mass outages, reportable data breaches, a loss of competitive advantage and fines and judgements. If malicious, wide-scale data destruction or theft of IP or other sensitive data may result.
extents.typical_case: The scope and size of incidents and outages are limited and responded to without lasting damage to the enterprise.
extents.best_case: Limited features/functions of systems are affected, quickly recovered and corrective action is immediately taken.

mitigating_controls.description: Communicate management objectives, direction and decisions made. Communicate awareness and promote understanding of alignment and I&T objectives to stakeholders throughout the enterprise. Communicate at regular intervals on important I&T-related decisions and their impact for the enterprise.

Define information (data) and system ownership. Define and maintain responsibilities for ownership of information (data) and information systems. Ensure that owners classify information and systems and protect them in line with their classification.

Define a data quality strategy. Define an integrated, enterprise-wide strategy to achieve and maintain the level of data quality (such as complexity, integrity, accuracy, completeness, validity, traceability and timeliness) required to support the business goals and objectives.

scenario_context.consequence: Business and customers may not be able to complete key processes impacting customer services.
scenario_context.timing: Business process supported by application may have critical processing times and periods (end of month) where outage would have greater impact. Time taken to identify outage, triage and fix issue may also impact other business process key timings. Need to implement an immediate fix may result in business process disruption. Timing for detection of the incident is also essential. Early detection may be useful in terms of incident response and minimization of impact on customers/relevant stakeholders. In this respect, proper controls (technical and organizational) and training of personnel are essential.

impact_dimensions.cost_of_response: The response may include increased handling costs to recheck that all hardware scheduled for decommission is clear of any data. If an external vendor is used or the hardware has already left the premises, the costs may be significant.
impact_dimensions.competitive_advantage: If the data are found by competitors to the enterprise, they could use it for their own benefit.
impact_dimensions.reputation: Reputation of the IT teams ability to successfully deliver solutions to the enterprise
impact_dimensions.fines_and_judgements: The data and information may be subject to privacy regulations resulting in a reportable incident and subsequent fines.

extents.worst_case: Worst-case scenario is the nondestroyed data will be accessible to either cybercriminals or corporate espionage and all confidential information would become public.
extents.typical_case: Most likely scenario is that once someone points out the issue with the decommissioning procedure, the procedure is updated accordingly to reflect the necessary destruction of data.
extents.best_case: Best-case scenario is the nondestroyed data that are totally harmless and there will be no negative impact to the enterprise.

mitigating_controls.description: Define architecture implementation. Create a viable implementation and migration plan in alignment with the program and project portfolios. Ensure the plan is closely coordinated to deliver value and that the required resources are available to complete the necessary work.
Define and prepare service agreements. Define and prepare service agreements based on options in the service catalogues. Include internal operational agreements.

Identify and evaluate vendor relationships and contracts. Continuously search for and identify vendors and categorize them into type, significance and criticality. Establish criteria to evaluate vendors and contracts. Review the overall portfolio of existing and alternative vendors and contracts.

Define and communicate the enterprises data management strategy and roles and responsibilities. Define how to manage and improve the enterprises data assets, in line with enterprise strategy and objectives. Communicate the data management strategy to all stakeholders. Assign roles and responsibilities to ensure that corporate data are managed as critical assets and the data management strategy is implemented and maintained in an effective and sustainable manner.

Define and maintain business functional and technical requirements. Based on the business case, identify, prioritize, specify and agree on business information, functional, technical and control requirements covering the scope/understanding of all initiatives required to achieve the expected outcomes of the proposed I&T-enabled business solution.

Build solutions. Install and configure solutions and integrate with business process activities. During configuration and integration of hardware and infrastructure software, implement control, security, privacy and auditability measures to protect resources and ensure availability and data integrity. Update the product or services catalogue to reflect the new solutions.

Manage the asset life cycle. Manage assets from procurement to disposal. Ensure that assets are utilized as effectively and efficiently as possible and are accounted for and physically protected until appropriately retired.

9M_Risk Scenario Vendor-Support-Ends.doc.title: Vendor support comes to an end for an I&T component
9M_Risk Scenario Vendor-Support-Ends.doc.statement: The vendor of a legacy system used by the enterprise has ceased all support for the system, resulting in total service interruption in case of a hardware defect or systems failure.
9M_Risk Scenario Vendor-Support-Ends.doc.oversight: I&T Governance Board Architecture Board Steering Committee (Programs/ Projects) Chief Risk Officer (CRO)

scenario_context.actor: Threat actor may be the third-party supplier, if vendor support has been terminated without adequate warning notice. If notice was supplied, the actors are insiders if there was awareness and no action taken.
scenario_context.intent: N/A
scenario_context.threat_event: The threat event occurs at the point when service support for the system ends. At this point, it remains a business risk, and there is no impact until a system malfunction occurs and cannot be rectified due to the lack of support.
scenario_context.assets: The assets at risk are those business processes and activities that are enabled by the system that is no longer supported.
scenario_context.consequence: Loss only occurs if a hardware defect or failure occurs; the lack of support does not in itself invoke a loss. Business processes and activities that are enabled by the system are no longer available if the hardware fails.
scenario_context.timing: Service interruption may relate to critical business process with critical processing times and periods (end of month) where delays have greater impact. Time taken to identify error, triage and identify alternate business process or fix issue may also impact business process key timings. Any need to implement a replacement may result in business process disruption during period of procurement and testing, and also at the point of implementation.

impact_dimensions.cost_of_response: Root cause investigation needs to be completed to identify and validate the cause of the disruption to business process. Alternative business process must be developed, pending hardware replacement.
impact_dimensions.competitive_advantage: N/A
impact_dimensions.reputation: N/A

extents.worst_case: Hardware defect results in total system shutdown with no alternate IT or business resilience available, and business processes are unable to be completed.
extents.typical_case: Alternative business processes are planned that can be used to bypass the system in the event of hardware failure, but these are untested; hence, the overall resilience of the business processes is uncertain. Ad-hoc arrangements (service extensions) have been agreed on with vendor for limited additional service support. Alternate business processes are planned but not tested or launched.
extents.best_case: Alternate business processes are available and in use that can be used to bypass the system in the event of hardware failure, and there is a funded project to remove the system from the IT estate.

mitigating_controls.description: EDM02.01 Establish the target investment mix. Review and ensure clarity of the enterprise and I&T strategies and current services. Define an appropriate investment mix based on cost, alignment with strategy, type of benefit for the programs in the portfolio, degree of risk, and financial measures such as cost and expected return on investment (ROI) over the full economic life cycle. Adjust the enterprise and I&T strategies where necessary.
APO09.05 Review service agreements and contracts. Conduct periodic reviews of the service agreements and revise when needed.

APO10.01 Identify and evaluate vendor relationships and contracts. Continuously search for and identify vendors and categorize them into type, significance and criticality. Establish criteria to evaluate vendors and contracts. Review the overall portfolio of existing and alternative vendors and contracts.

APO10.04 Manage vendor risk. Identify and manage risk relating to vendors ability to continually provide secure, efficient and effective service delivery. This also includes the subcontractors or upstream vendors that are relevant in the service delivery of the direct vendor.

BAI04.01 Assess current availability, performance and capacity, and create a baseline. Assess availability, performance and capacity of services and resources to ensure that cost-justifiable capacity and performance are available to support business needs and deliver against service-level agreements (SLAs). Create availability, performance and capacity baselines for future comparison.
BAI09.02 Manage critical assets. Identify assets that are critical in providing service capability. Maximize their reliability and availability to support business needs.

BAI04.02 Assess business impact. Identify important services to the enterprise. Map services and resources to business processes and identify business dependencies. Ensure that the impact of unavailable resources is fully agreed on and accepted by the customer. For vital business functions, ensure that availability requirements can be satisfied per service-level agreement (SLA).

DSS04.02 Maintain business resilience. Evaluate business resilience options and choose a cost-effective and viable strategy that will ensure enterprise continuity, disaster recovery and incident response in the face of a disaster or other major incident or disruption.
